observations: body L1-L6: the figure stands on the right of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the semicircle AZB about the centre of the Earth E (radius 59.9 pt) with its diameter AB, the Earth, a small semicircle through F (radius 20.9 pt), the vertical EZ and the lines FL and EL, which end at the circle 0.7 pt short of their meeting point; LF produced to Q and the perpendicular QE are dashed. The centres of the two semicircles lie within 0.6 pt of E. The letters F and Q print italic, the others upright; the A is printed without its bar.

body L1-L9: in the right triangle EQL, sin FLE = R EQ : EL; in the right triangle EQF the angle QFE is the vertical angle of ZFL = ζ, and EF = a; so dist. × sin p = a sin ζ, which is the law of sines in the triangle EFL. With a = 1 it is al-Battānī's first rule, p. 85, L19-L22: the sine of the apparent zenith distance multiplied by R and divided by the sine of the parallax converted into minutes, that is by 60 sin p, R being 60. In L5 the commas after the fractions stand high, beside the tops of the denominators.
body L8, L18: «al–Battānī» is letter-spaced, with long dashes (5.3 and 5.6 pt).

body L10-L15: the figure stands on the left of these lines and is redrawn from the print: the semicircle AZB about E (radius 72.7 pt), the Earth through F (radius 24.6 pt), the vertical EZ and the lines FL and EL, as in the first figure; the perpendicular FQ on EL is dashed (four dashes), and an arc of ten dots about E (radius 44.7 pt) from EZ to EL marks the angle z; the letter z stands on it. The letters L and E print upright, the others italic.

body L10-L19: by the law of sines in the triangle EFL, FL = a sin z : sin p; QL = FL cos p, and taking QL = FL neglects at most 1/6600 of FL for p up to 1°; EQ = a cos z : R; so the distance is a sin z : sin p + a cos z : R, and with a = 1 and cos z = sin h it is (β), the second rule of p. 85, L23-L27, which Nallino restored there in brackets (note 4 there: the whole period is missing in the codex and in Plato). A heavy bracket opens Schiaparelli's addition in L10 and closes it in L21.

body L20-L21: «23–24» has a long dash (5.4 pt), and the dash before «Schiaparelli» measures 9.1 pt. The words struck out stand in Nallino's restoration of the second rule (p. 85, L23-L24), which repeats the wording of the first; formula (β) divides the sine of z by the sine of p without the factor R.
body L22-L23: the head of the commentary on chapter 41; the dash after «a)» measures 10.2 pt, and «37–39» has a long dash (5.3 pt).
body L24-L35: the place is p. 85, L37-L39, the beginning of chapter 41 on the visibility of the new moon. «ash–shakk» (L29) has a long dash (5.6 pt); the ‘ayn of «sha‘bān» (L27) is the turned comma.

notes_right L1-L2: Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXV) add to this note a reference on the announcement of the new moon among the Jews, who did not accept the testimony of women, slaves and the wicked: Maimonides, de novilunio, chapter II, col. 240-244 of the edition cited in the preface, p. XXXIV, note 3. The note goes on to p. 266.
notes_right L1: the print sets no rule between the two columns of the notes.
